source_gaps.description: The standalone machine-readable Continuum v1.2 core implementation artifact referenced by the deep-research report is not present in the repository, conversation files, or Library, and the corpus search is exhaustive: across all four distinct source documents only 3 of the 25 v1.2-named tables carry DDL. The original is treated as unrecoverable, so issue #2's first close criterion is unreachable. A DERIVED replacement with per-declaration provenance is committed under docs/spec/ (FND-SPEC-001) and is CI-verified against PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector. RESOLVED under issue #2's second criterion by FND-SPEC-002. Read that criterion carefully before relying on this: it is a conjunction -- reconstructed from authoritative source material AND approved through an ADR -- and all three clauses are answered on the ADR-APPROVAL half ONLY, not the authoritative-source half. For a genuine [DECISION] there is no source to reconstruct from; that is what the tag means. ADR-0007 states every activity timeout has no source to appeal to, and ADR-0010 states each residual schema declaration is one v1.2 does not support. The resolution rests on issue #2's own build policy, which directs that additional choices be marked as an ADR decision RATHER THAN presented as recovered source text; under the alternative reading, requiring both halves for every item, no [DECISION] could ever satisfy criterion 2 and this gap would be permanently unclosable. That choice was put to the repository owner, who selected the build-policy reading. Coverage is mechanical: every [DECISION] maps to an accepted ADR, verified by scripts/check_decision_coverage.py. The version clause is narrower again -- ADR-0008 approves the pinning rule rather than inventing versions for six libraries nothing imports yet. Full reasoning in docs/implementation/evidence/FND-SPEC-002.md. Reopen if either reading is rejected.
